# Tovuk agent guide

Tovuk deploys Rust workers, static frontends, and full-stack services.
Full-stack services use one root tovuk.toml, serve the frontend at `/`, and route
`/api/*` to the Rust worker.

Use the native CLI after installing it with npm, Homebrew, PyPI, or Cargo:

```sh
tovuk check --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk account update --handle <handle> --display-name <name> --json
tovuk deploy --dry-run --json
tovuk deploy --wait --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk deploy list --json
tovuk deploy show <deploy_id> --json
tovuk deploy cancel <deploy_id> --json
```

Reference: [Tovuk docs](https://docs.tovuk.com).

Resource references:

- `docs/reference/project-contract.mdx`: tovuk.toml workflow, required files, kind and capabilities, local checks, dry-run planning, build commands, and Rust/static runtime policy.
- `docs/reference/workers.mdx`: Rust Worker deploy workflow, account setup, dry-run review, post-deploy Service snapshots, HTTP/API routing, runtime events, WebSocket upgrades, and frontend policy.
- `docs/reference/resources.mdx`: Service Resources account setup,
  post-deploy Service snapshots, CLI/API/dashboard parity, resource routes,
  and runtime bindings.
- `docs/reference/sqlite.mdx`: SQLite account setup, Service context, commands, limits, backups, and query metrics.
- `docs/reference/state.mdx`: State account setup, Service context, keyed objects, storage, and alarms.
- `docs/reference/kv.mdx`: KV account setup, Service context, commands, API routes, meters, and limits.
- `docs/reference/queues.mdx`: queue account setup, Service context, producers, consumers, retries, and dead letters.
- `docs/reference/cron.mdx`: Cron account setup, Service context, scheduled Rust worker events, and trigger lifecycle commands.
- `docs/reference/bindings.mdx`: Service Binding account setup, Service context, private calls, and runtime binding environment names.
- `docs/reference/secrets.mdx`: account setup, Service context, and server-only environment values.
- `docs/reference/storage.mdx`: Object Storage account setup, Service context, uploads, downloads, multipart, and egress.
- `docs/reference/domains.mdx`: Custom Domain account setup, Service context, DNS records, verification, and cleanup.
- `docs/reference/logs-builds.mdx`: `tovuk check --json`, account setup, dry-run, service snapshots before history and after repair redeploys, returned `build_job.id`/`final_build.status`, build/deploy/service logs, and queued deploy cancellation.
- `docs/reference/limits.mdx`: deployment guardrails, account setup, plan-limit recovery, and paid usage caps.
- `docs/reference/products.mdx`: product catalog fields, account setup, dry-run, usage, and usage-cap selection workflow.
- `docs/reference/packages.mdx`: install channels, account setup checks,
  post-deploy Service snapshots, package parity, and native binary recovery.
- `docs/reference/usage-caps.mdx`: account setup and hard caps for every public meter.

Workflow references:

- `docs/index.mdx`: docs start page, path chooser, package install snippet
  with account setup check, and visible Copy prompt with check, account setup,
  dry-run, wait deploy, and post-deploy Service snapshot commands for AI coding
  agents.
- `docs/quickstart.mdx`: first Rust worker or full-stack deploy flow with a
  post-deploy Service snapshot.
- `docs/deploy.mdx`: check, account setup, dry-run, deploy, service snapshot, deploy history, cancellation, and recovery.
- `docs/production-readiness.mdx`: production launch workflow, account setup,
  usage caps, post-deploy Service snapshots, deploy evidence, status
  distinction, secrets, domains, and cleanup.
- `docs/agents.mdx`: agent deploy workflow, reusable deploy and starter
  prompts with account checks, post-deploy Service snapshots, recovery,
  support, and abuse workflow.
- `docs/pricing.mdx`: pricing, account setup, usage limits, cost estimates, and hard caps.
- `docs/templates.mdx`: project templates, `tovuk new`, starter account
  checks, post-deploy Service snapshots, and starter workflows.
- `docs/changelog.mdx`: dated changes, fixes, and release-note review links.

Operational references:

- `docs/status.mdx`: `/health`, `/healthz`, `/v1/status`, the CLI `api_unreachable` payload, and project-failure handoff to logs.
- `docs/support.mdx`: support ticket evidence, account setup, service snapshot, Dashboard Support, and support CLI/API routes.
- `docs/abuse.mdx`: public abuse reports, account setup for owner-visible reports, owner appeals, operator quarantine, and abuse rate limits.

Dashboard Overview is available at `https://tovuk.com/account` and shows
Service kind, per-Service resource counts for SQLite, Object Storage, KV,
Queues, Cron, State, Service Bindings, Secrets, and Custom Domains, plus
enabled and disabled capability summaries and
copyable `tovuk service show <service> --json`,
`tovuk logs --service <service> --limit 100 --json`,
`tovuk storage list --service <service> --json`,
`tovuk limits set worker_requests --period day --value 100000 --notify-at-percent 80 --json`,
`tovuk support create "Service issue" ... --service <service> --json`, and
`tovuk service delete <service> --json` commands.

Dashboard Usage is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/usage` and supports
the same cap set and remove actions as `tovuk limits`, plus the same hosted
checkout flow as `tovuk billing checkout --json` and billing portal flow as
`tovuk billing portal`. Usage rows show copyable `tovuk limits set` commands with `--notify-at-percent` and copyable `tovuk limits delete` commands for the selected meter.

Dashboard Resources is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/resources` and
supports creating and deleting SQLite, KV, Queue, Cron, State, and Service
Binding resources through the same API routes as the CLI. It can also run
single SQLite queries and shows returned rows, `rowsRead`, `rowsWritten`,
`vmSteps`, `fullscanSteps`, storage, duration, and next actions. It can list
SQLite backups, create SQLite backups, and restore SQLite backups through the
same API routes as the CLI. It can list KV keys, read one KV key, write one KV
key, and delete one KV key with `kv_lists`,
`kv_reads`, `kv_writes`, `kv_deletes`, and `kv_storage_bytes` metering. It can
update Queue retries, retention, batch size, batch timeout, and dead-letter
Queue settings, read Queue messages, read Queue metrics, send one Queue message,
and send one Queue batch with `queue_operations` metering.
It can update Cron schedules, pause Cron triggers, and resume Cron triggers
through the same API routes as the CLI. It can list State objects, list State
keys, read State values, write State values, delete State values, read State
alarms, set State alarms, and delete State alarms with `state_requests`,
`state_duration_gb_milliseconds`, `state_sqlite_rows_read`,
`state_sqlite_rows_written`, and
`state_sqlite_storage_bytes` metering. Use CLI bulk commands for bulk KV reads,
writes, and removals.

Dashboard Secrets is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/secrets` and
supports listing, setting, and deleting write-only service secrets through the
same API routes as `tovuk env`.

Dashboard Storage is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/storage` and
`https://tovuk.com/<handle>/storage`. It lists objects, uploads ordinary files,
automatically uses multipart transfer above 100 MiB, creates download URLs, and
deletes objects through the same API routes and limits as the CLI. Use
`tovuk storage upload --json` when an agent needs local-file automation outside
the browser.

Dashboard Activity is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/activity` and
shows recent deploys, builds, runtime logs, next actions, and copyable repair
commands through the same activity, deploy cancel, and log API routes as the
CLI. Queued deploy rows can cancel queued build work and expose the same
`tovuk deploy cancel <deploy_id> --json` command.

Agent repair loop:

1. Run `tovuk check --json`.
2. If it fails, read the first failed check.
3. Apply its `agent_instruction` exactly.
4. Rerun check until it passes.
5. Run `tovuk account show --json`.
6. If account setup is incomplete, run
   `tovuk account update --handle <handle> --display-name <name> --json`.
7. Run `tovuk deploy --dry-run --json`.
8. Review warnings, enabled and disabled capabilities, `missingConfig`,
   `requiredFixes`, meters, `meterPlan`, limits, and `billingEstimate`.
9. Set hard usage caps for expected load.
10. Run `tovuk deploy --wait --json`.
11. Inspect the Service snapshot with `tovuk service show <service> --json`.
12. Inspect deploy history with `tovuk deploy list --json` or
   `tovuk deploy show <deploy_id> --json` when needed.
13. If a newer deploy supersedes queued work, run `tovuk deploy cancel <deploy_id> --json`.
14. If deploy fails, read `build_job.id` or the failed build id.
15. Run `tovuk logs --build <build_id> --json`.
16. Fix the first actionable log error.
17. Rerun `tovuk check --json` and `tovuk deploy --dry-run --json`.
18. Run `tovuk deploy --wait --json` after the fix.
19. Inspect the Service snapshot again with `tovuk service show <service> --json`
    before reading more build or deploy logs.

Rust worker contract:

- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `tovuk.toml` are committed.
- `kind = "rust_worker"` is set in `tovuk.toml`.
- `[capabilities]` explicitly sets `worker = true`,
  `static_frontend = false`, service capabilities to true, and unused optional
  resources to false.
- `[build].check` includes `cargo fmt --all --check`.
- `[build].check` includes release-mode
  `cargo check --locked --release --all-targets --all-features`.
- `[build].check` includes release-mode
  `cargo test --locked --release --all-targets --all-features`.
- `[build].check` includes
  `cargo clippy --locked --release --all-targets --all-features` with
  `-D warnings`, `-D clippy::all`, `-D clippy::pedantic`, panic/unwrap bans,
  and resource lints such as `large_futures`, `large_stack_frames`,
  `mem_forget`, and `redundant_clone`.
- `[resources].memory` is `128mb`.
- `[resources].cpu` is `1`; set `worker_cpu_ms` usage caps for CPU budget.
- `[resources].idle_timeout_minutes` stays between `1` and `60`.
- The server listens on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- The configured health path returns HTTP 200.
- Direct `unsafe` is not allowed in workspace source.
- Deploy archives contain source files only, not generated directories, secret
  files, or compiled artifacts such as `.exe`, `.so`, `.dylib`, `.jar`,
  `.node`, and `.rlib`.

Static frontend contract:

- `kind = "static_frontend"` is set in `tovuk.toml`.
- `[capabilities]` explicitly sets `static_frontend = true`,
  `worker = false`, service capabilities to true, and unused optional
  resources to false.
- Package static frontends commit `package.json` and a package lockfile.
- Package browser source is `.ts` or `.tsx` under `src`, `app`, `pages`,
  `routes`, or `components`.
- Package `package.json` has `typecheck`, `lint`, and `build` scripts.
- Package `typecheck` runs stable native type-aware TypeScript checks such as
  `oxlint --type-aware --type-check`.
- Package `lint` runs native tooling such as `oxlint` or `biome check`.
- Package `lint` also runs Fallow `dead-code`, semantic `dupes`, and `health`
  gates.
- Package `[build].check` installs dependencies and runs package scripts for
  typecheck and lint.
- Plain static frontends without `package.json` include `index.html`, set
  `[build].check = ":"`, `[build].command = ":"`, and `[build].output = "."`.
- Weak typecheck, fake lint, missing Fallow quality gates, and JavaScript-based
  lint/format scripts are rejected for package deploys.
- JavaScript and TypeScript are frontend-only. API routes, SSR handlers,
  middleware, and server logic must move to the Rust worker.

Full-stack contract:

- One root `tovuk.toml` sets `kind = "fullstack"`.
- `[capabilities]` explicitly sets `static_frontend = true`, `worker = true`,
  service capabilities to true, and unused optional resources to false.
- `[worker].root` points to the Rust worker.
- `[frontend].root` points to the static frontend.
- The frontend calls same-origin `/api`.
- The worker health path is `/api/healthz`.
- Worker build and runtime commands must use `cargo build --release` and a
  `./target/release/*` Rust binary, never Node, Bun, Deno, or TS runtimes.
- Queue handlers are Rust worker routes at `POST /.tovuk/queues/<queue>`.
- Queue batch size, batch timeout, retries, retention, and dead-letter routing
  are configurable through the CLI/API.
- Queue handler payloads contain base64 message bodies. Return `2xx` only after
  the batch is safely handled.
- Cron handlers are Rust worker routes at `POST /.tovuk/cron/<trigger>`.
- Cron handlers must be idempotent because schedules can overlap with retries
  or manual agent actions.
- WebSocket upgrades on worker routes are proxied to Rust workers and meter
  response-side tunnel bytes as `worker_transfer_bytes`.

Useful commands:

```sh
tovuk pricing --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk deploy --dry-run --json
curl https://api.tovuk.com/v1/status
tovuk usage --json
tovuk service list --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk service delete <service> --json
tovuk logs --build <build_id> --json
tovuk logs --service <service> --json
tovuk env list --service <service> --json
tovuk domains list --service <service> --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk sqlite create --service <service> DB --json
tovuk sqlite query --service <service> DB "select 1" --json
tovuk sqlite backup create --service <service> DB --json
tovuk sqlite backup list --service <service> DB --json
tovuk sqlite backup restore --service <service> DB sqlite_backup_1 --json
tovuk sqlite delete --service <service> DB --json
tovuk kv create --service <service> CACHE --json
tovuk kv namespace delete --service <service> CACHE --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk queue create --service <service> failed_jobs --json
tovuk queue create --service <service> jobs --max-batch-size 10 --max-batch-timeout-seconds 5 --dead-letter-queue failed_jobs --json
tovuk queue update --service <service> jobs --max-batch-size 25 --json
tovuk queue update --service <service> jobs --clear-dead-letter-queue --json
tovuk queue delete --service <service> jobs --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk cron create --service <service> nightly "0 0 * * *" --json
tovuk cron update --service <service> nightly "*/15 * * * *" --json
tovuk cron disable --service <service> nightly --json
tovuk cron enable --service <service> nightly --json
tovuk cron delete --service <service> nightly --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk state create --service <service> Room --json
tovuk state objects --service <service> Room --json
tovuk state keys --service <service> Room room-1 --json
tovuk state put --service <service> Room room-1 counter 1 --json
tovuk state get --service <service> Room room-1 counter --json
tovuk state alarm set --service <service> Room room-1 --delay-seconds 60 --json
tovuk state alarm get --service <service> Room room-1 --json
tovuk state alarm delete --service <service> Room room-1 --json
tovuk state delete --service <service> Room --json
tovuk account show --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk binding create --service <service> AUTH_SERVICE --target auth-service --json
tovuk binding delete --service <service> AUTH_SERVICE --json
tovuk limits set worker_requests --period day --value 100000 --notify-at-percent 80 --json
tovuk limits set state_requests --period month --value 1000000 --notify-at-percent 80 --json
tovuk limits set state_sqlite_rows_written --period month --value 50000000 --notify-at-percent 80 --json
tovuk limits delete worker_requests --period day --json
tovuk storage list --service <service> --json
tovuk storage upload --service <service> ./file.png uploads/file.png --public --json
tovuk storage download --service <service> uploads/file.png ./file.png --json
tovuk storage url --service <service> uploads/file.png --json
tovuk storage delete --service <service> uploads/file.png --json
tovuk billing checkout --json
tovuk billing portal
tovuk account show --json
tovuk support list --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk support create "Deploy failed" "Agent retried deploy after check." --service <service> --build <build_id> --deploy <deploy_id> --failing-command "tovuk deploy --wait --json" --first-log-line "first actionable log line" --json
tovuk support resolve <ticket_id> --json
tovuk abuse report https://demo.tovuk.app "Phishing page" "Credential collection form" --category phishing --reporter-email reporter@example.com --evidence "Screenshot URL and request id" --json
tovuk abuse list --json
tovuk abuse list --operator --json
tovuk abuse appeal abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Removed the reported file and rotated credentials." --evidence "deploy_1 remediation log" --json
tovuk abuse triage abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Reviewed reporter evidence and target service metadata." --json
tovuk abuse notify-owner abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Owner-visible report recorded with evidence summary." --json
tovuk abuse quarantine abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Confirmed malware object and preserved scanner evidence." --json
tovuk abuse resolve abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Reporter issue remediated and clean deploy verified." --json
tovuk abuse reject abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Evidence did not match the reported target." --json
tovuk abuse release abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Owner removed object and redeployed clean build." --json
```

Without `--json`, `tovuk service list` prints a compact table with Service
kind, runtime status, URL, enabled and disabled capabilities, and resource
counts. `tovuk service show` prints a compact Service snapshot with
capabilities, resource counts, usage, latest deploy, latest build, and next
actions. Agents should still use `--json` for machine parsing.

Dashboard Overview is available at `https://tovuk.com/account` and
`https://tovuk.com/<handle>`. When no Services exist, it shows first Service
commands for `tovuk new hello-service --template fullstack-rust-tanstack`,
`cd hello-service/web`, `bun install`, `cd ..`, `tovuk check --json`,
`tovuk deploy --dry-run --json`, and `tovuk deploy --wait --json`. The
committed `tovuk.toml` remains the source of
truth; agents should still use CLI and API commands for automation. Service
rows expose enabled and disabled capability summaries plus
`tovuk service show <service> --json`,
`tovuk logs --service <service> --limit 100 --json`,
`tovuk storage list --service <service> --json`,
`tovuk limits set worker_requests --period day --value 100000 --notify-at-percent 80 --json`,
`tovuk support create "Service issue" ... --service <service> --json`,
`tovuk service delete <service> --json`, and the same `DELETE /v1/services/{service_id}`
cleanup action for smoke-test Services.

Dashboard Support is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/support` and uses
the same ticket API and rate limits as the CLI. Ticket rows expose copyable
`tovuk support list --json`, `tovuk support resolve <ticket_id> --json`,
`tovuk service show <service> --json`, and
`tovuk logs --build <build_id> --json` commands when context exists.

Dashboard Abuse is available at `https://tovuk.com/account/abuse` and uses the
same abuse report, list, and appeal API routes and rate limits as the CLI.
Owner agents should confirm account setup with `tovuk account show --json`
before owner-visible list or appeal work. Report rows expose copyable `tovuk abuse list --json`,
`tovuk abuse appeal <report_id> "Remediation details" --json`, and
`tovuk service show <service> --json` commands when report state supports them.

`tovuk storage upload` automatically switches to multipart transfer for files
larger than 100 MiB. Object storage limits expose object size, part count,
metadata size, custom domains per storage bucket, bucket management operations,
and same-key write throughput.

Before load tests, production launch, or paid usage, run
`tovuk pricing --json`, confirm account setup with `tovuk account show --json`,
inspect `tovuk deploy --dry-run --json` and `tovuk usage --json`, then set hard
usage caps with `tovuk limits set`.
Useful cap metrics include `build_minutes`, `worker_requests`, `worker_cpu_ms`,
`sqlite_rows_read`, `sqlite_rows_written`, `kv_reads`, `queue_operations`,
`state_requests`, `state_duration_gb_milliseconds`, `state_sqlite_rows_read`,
`state_sqlite_rows_written`,
`object_storage_bytes`, `object_storage_class_a_operations`, and
`object_storage_class_b_operations`, and `object_storage_egress_bytes`.

`tovuk pricing --json` exposes a `products` catalog. Use each product's
`features`, `meters`, `meter_details`, `pricing_fields`, and `limit_fields`
before load tests, media uploads, or paid usage.
`tovuk deploy --dry-run --json` is read-only and combines `tovuk.toml`, quality checks,
capability meters, account limits, usage, and `billingEstimate` before deploy.
Each service includes `missingConfig` for `tovuk.toml` repair, `requiredFixes`
for every failed quality check, and `meterPlan` entries for enabled service
meters with meter units, pricing fields, limit fields, and ready-to-fill
`tovuk limits set` cap commands.
The catalog includes Worker, Static Frontend, SQLite, Object Storage, State,
KV, Queues, Cron, Service Bindings, Secrets, Custom Domains, Logs, Builds, and
Usage Caps.

Use `GET /v1/status` only when Tovuk itself appears unavailable. If a Tovuk CLI
command returns `api_unreachable`, retry it, then check `/v1/status` before
changing project code. If the API is available and a deploy fails, inspect build
logs instead of changing status checks.

Never print or commit secrets. Put secrets in Tovuk env vars with
`tovuk env set --service <service> KEY=value`.

When a free-tier limit blocks work, confirm account setup with
`tovuk account show --json`, inspect `tovuk usage --json`, then run
`tovuk billing checkout --json` when payment is the blocker and show the
returned URL to the human. For invoices, payment methods, or subscription
changes, run `tovuk billing portal` and show the returned URL to the human.
When Tovuk support is needed, create a ticket only after collecting the
failing command, service id, build id, deploy id, first actionable log line,
and what the agent already tried. Resolve the ticket when the issue is fixed
so future agents do not duplicate the same support work.
